summary: Backend-only regression verification of the @Devils_gods fixes (HTML-in-200 auth detection + WHM-root fallback for 6 file routes + subdomain/addon fallback). Re-ran all 3 new test files from scratch: ALL PASS (4/4, 7/7, 6/6 assertions). Static wiring verified in js/cpanel-routes.js (6 routes) and js/cpanel-proxy.js (4 API2 functions + uapi HTML detector). Full regression sweep (node js/tests cpanel suites + full jest suite, 379 tests) shows ZERO new regressions — every failure is byte-identical to the `git stash` baseline on unmodified cpanel-proxy.js/cpanel-routes.js. Node service restarted with new code: supervisor RUNNING, /api/health healthy+DB connected (internal :5000 and external pod URL). Found ONE real coverage gap (api2() has no HTML-in-200 detector — see backend_issues.minor + RCA).

minor.issue: COVERAGE GAP: the new 'HTTP 200 + cPanel login-page HTML' detector was added only to uapi(). api2() and the four direct-axios SubDomain/AddonDomain calls still parse res.data?.cpanelresult on a 200-HTML body, yielding {status:0, errors:['Operation failed']} with NO code:'CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE' and no httpStatus. Verified with a mocked-axios probe: renameFile() → {"status":0,"data":[],"errors":["Operation failed"]} and the route-level _isAuthBroken() equivalent returns FALSE, so the WHM-root fallback would NOT fire for that failure mode. Production evidence for @Devils_gods was a hard 403 (which IS covered), so this is a robustness gap, not a live blocker.

Steps 2 & 3 ($pull from cpanelAccounts.addonDomains + Cloudflare record/worker cleanup) run unconditionally even when cpProxy.removeAddonDomain() returned status:0, and the route replies HTTP 200 with the failure body. If the cPanel-side removal (incl. WHM fallback) fails, the domain disappears from our tracking + CF while still attached in cPanel — the exact 'i cant delete that domain' class of orphan state. Consider gating DB/CF cleanup on status===1 (or explicitly on 'already gone' errors) and returning a non-200 on hard failure.

Test noise only: prints '⚠️ CRITICAL: SESSION_SECRET not set! ... passwords will be lost on restart!' because the test doesn't load dotenv before requiring cpanel-auth. Harmless (test mints its own JWT and passes) but the scary log can mask real output.

action_items: Optional hardening: hoist the HTML-in-200 login-page detector into a shared helper and apply it in api2() (and in the 4 direct-axios SubDomain/AddonDomain success paths) so fileop/subdomain/addon also normalise to code:'CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE' and trigger the WHM-root fallback.
Review /api/panel/domains/remove: do not unpersist Mongo addonDomains / wipe Cloudflare records when the cPanel removal failed, and return a non-200 status on hard failure.
Optional: load dotenv (or set SESSION_SECRET) at the top of test_cpanel_routes_file_ops_whm_fallback.js to silence the misleading CRITICAL warning.
critical_code_review_comments: Wiring verified: _isAuthBroken (l.175), _uapiViaWhmRoot (l.197), _fileopViaWhmRoot (l.221) each declared exactly once, immediately after _isAuthBroken. Fallback branches present at /files/content (685), /files/save (713), /files/rename (1196), /files/compress (1285), /files/copy (1317), /files/move (1350) — all guarded by `result?.status !== 1 && _isAuthBroken(result)`, all wrapped in try/catch, all log a fallback line, all no-op when whmApi is null (missing WHM_TOKEN).

cpanel-proxy.js verified: uapi() HTML-in-200 detector at l.404-420 returns {status:0, code:'CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE', data:null, httpStatus}; _resolveWhmBaseUrl (523) + _api2ViaWhmRoot (532) declared once; createSubdomain (1031), deleteSubdomain (1075), addAddonDomain (867), removeAddonDomain (909) all call _api2ViaWhmRoot inside catch when looksLikeAuthFailure(status, err.message).

_api2ViaWhmRoot returns {status:1,...} on success, matching what all callers check (result?.status === 1 in js/_index.js:15587, cpanel-job-handlers.js:181, cpanel-routes.js:1439) — no caller-shape mismatch.
js/cpanel-routes.js is 3474 lines — well over the 700-line guideline; File Manager routes are a natural module to split out.
_makeWhmApi does require('https')/require('axios') inside the function on every call — cheap (module cache) but should be hoisted for clarity.

success_rate.backend: 100% of the 17 new-fix assertions pass (3/3 target test files green); 0 new regressions across 128 js/tests cpanel suites sampled + 379 jest tests

seed_data_creation: None. No writes to the live Railway Mongo. All tests use monkey-patched axios. BOT_ENVIRONMENT stayed 'development', SKIP_WEBHOOK_SYNC stayed 'true'. No cPanel/addon-domain mutations on live accounts.
test_credentials: Read /app/memory/test_credentials.md — no email/password auth in this app (Telegram chatId based). Panel routes correctly return 401 {"error":"Unauthorized"} without a JWT (verified on the external pod URL for GET /api/panel/files/content and POST /api/panel/files/move).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Confirmed-pre-existing (NOT regressions, byte-identical on `git stash` baseline of js/cpanel-proxy.js + js/cpanel-routes.js): test_cpanel_proxy_down.js 2 fails (listFiles admin-notified-once, throttle window); test_cpanel_health.js 2 fails (onDown/onUp transition events); test_file_delete_folder_fix.js 3 fails (deleteFile killdir-vs-unlink, handleDelete exists in FileManager.js, confirm message wording); jest tests/: 6 suites / 12 tests fail (azure-provider, callrecon_notify_fix, ivr_parity, os-aware-provider-routing, wallet-deposit-reverted-to-amount-first, whm_health_probe — several are worker crashes / 'suite must contain at least one test'). Green: test_cpanel_proxy_retry, test_cpanel_tunnel_routing, test_delete_folder_op, test_addon_from_bot (94/94). Run js/tests/*.js with plain `node` (jest.config testMatch only covers /app/tests/*.test.js).
rca_of_the_issue: Fix under test is correct for the reported failure modes. Root cause reconfirmed: user-level cPanel HTTP Basic Auth is broken for cpUser auth62f9, so cpsrvd either returns 403 'Access denied' (API2 fileop → move/rename/copy/compress) or HTTP 200 with the cPanel login page HTML (UAPI Fileman::get_file_content → '<!DOCTYPE html>' rendered in the editor). Both are now normalised to code:'CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE' (uapi HTML detector) / detected via httpStatus 401|403 + looksLikeAuthFailure, and every affected route retries through WHM-root impersonation (WHM_TOKEN + cpanel_jsonapi_user). Residual risk: the HTML-in-200 variant is still undetected inside api2() and the direct-axios subdomain/addon calls, so if cpsrvd starts answering 200-HTML (instead of 403) for fileop or addon-domain delete, the fallback will not fire and the user sees a generic 'Operation failed'.
